adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — Deploying this SET-to-ZSET change without migration or dual reads makes active predeploy segment keys raise Redis WRONGTYPE errors and stall span processing until they expire.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a change from Redis SET commands (sadd, scard, sscan, sunionstore) to ZSET commands (zadd, zcard, zscan, zunionstore) in buffer.py. The Lua script in add-buffer.lua also changes from scard/sunionstore to zcard/zunionstore. However, there's no migration logic or dual-read capability shown in the diff. If this code is deployed while there are existing keys in Redis that were created as SETs (before the change), calling ZSET operations like zcard or zscan on those SET keys will cause Redis WRONGTYPE errors ('WRONGTYPE Operation against a key holding the wrong kind of value'). This would break span processing for any in-flight segments until those old SET keys expire.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py:123 — The tests never exceed 1000 spans or assert score-ordered eviction, so the new bounded-insert path can fail while CI remains green.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a new bounded-insert path in add-buffer.lua that limits spans to 1000 using zpopmin when span_count > 1000. Looking at the test file changes, all tests add only 4-6 spans each and none test the eviction behavior when exceeding 1000 spans. The finding correctly identifies that this new code path (the bounded insert with score-ordered eviction via zpopmin) has no test coverage. This is a legitimate missing test concern for newly added nontrivial logic, not a bug itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — Switching live span keys from Redis sets to sorted sets makes zadd fail with WRONGTYPE until every pre-deploy set key expires.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a migration from Redis sets (sadd, scard, sscan, sunionstore) to sorted sets (zadd, zcard, zscan, zunionstore) in buffer.py and add-buffer.lua. The finding correctly identifies that during deployment, existing keys created with set commands (sadd) will still exist in Redis. When the new code tries to use sorted set commands (zadd) on these existing set keys, Redis will return a WRONGTYPE error because you cannot use sorted set operations on regular set data types. This is a real deployment/migration bug - the code doesn't handle the transition period where old set keys coexist with new sorted set expectations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 — Reducing redirect traversal from 10000 to 1000 leaves deeper trace trees split into separate buffers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows the loop limit being reduced from 10000 to 1000 at line 30. The original comment stated 'theoretically this limit means that segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly.' By reducing this to 1000, trace trees deeper than 1000 levels would now be split into separate buffers instead of being properly joined. This is a real architectural concern - while 1000 is likely sufficient for most use cases, it's a behavioral change that could affect edge cases with very deep traces. The finding correctly identifies this tradeoff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:62 — The fixed 1000 eviction limit ignores SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans, so deployments configured with another limit silently change capacity behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a hardcoded limit of 1000 in the Lua script (line 62: `if span_count > 1000 then redis.call('zpopmin', set_key, span_count - 1000)`), while the Python code in buffer.py has a configurable `max_segment_spans` parameter (visible in the removed code around line 446-452 that checked `if len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans`). The finding correctly identifies that the Lua script's hardcoded 1000 limit doesn't respect the configurable Python setting, which could cause inconsistent behavior. However, this is a design/architecture concern rather than a bug since the code will still function - it just may not respect custom configurations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:845 — OptimizedCursorPaginator copies BasePaginator.get_result almost verbatim, so future fixes to cursor construction or filtering can silently diverge between the two paths.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows OptimizedCursorPaginator (lines 818-912) implements get_result with nearly identical logic to the existing BasePaginator.get_result shown in the diff (lines 176-195). The finding correctly identifies that this code duplication creates a maintenance risk where future bug fixes to cursor construction or filtering in one class may not be applied to the other. This is a legitimate architectural/scope concern about the new code introduced in this diff, not a bug but a real maintainability issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — The full subsegment is materialized and sent to Redis before eviction runs, so an oversized batch can still create an unbounded ZADD request and transient sorted-set allocation.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in buffer.py line 197, `p.zadd(set_key, {span.payload: span.end_timestamp_precise for span in subsegment})` sends the entire subsegment to Redis in a single ZADD call. The eviction logic (zpopmin when span_count > 1000) only runs in the Lua script (add-buffer.lua) AFTER the data is already stored. This means if a subsegment has thousands of spans, the full batch is materialized and sent to Redis before any size limiting occurs, creating unbounded memory allocation both client-side (building the dict) and server-side (the ZADD operation). The finding correctly identifies this as a potential issue where oversized batches bypass the intended 1000-span limit during the initial write.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — Deploying this SET-to-ZSET change against unexpired span-buf keys makes zadd/zscan and the Lua zcard fail with WRONGTYPE, halting affected consumer/flush batches until TTL expiry.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a migration from Redis SET commands (sadd, scard, sscan, sunionstore) to ZSET commands (zadd, zcard, zscan, zunionstore) in buffer.py and add-buffer.lua. The keys use the same naming pattern 'span-buf:s:{project_and_trace}:span_id'. If this code is deployed while existing SET-type keys from the old implementation still exist in Redis (before their TTL expires), calling ZSET operations like zadd, zcard, zscan on SET-type keys will cause Redis WRONGTYPE errors. This is a real deployment/migration bug - there's no migration strategy shown in the diff to handle the transition period.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:60 — No test covers inserting over 1000 spans to verify eviction retains the newest spans and enforces the cap

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new logic in add-buffer.lua (lines 55-61) that enforces a 1000 span cap by evicting spans when the count exceeds 1000 using zpopmin. This is new, nontrivial logic that affects data retention behavior. The finding correctly identifies that no test in the diff covers this eviction scenario - the test files show spans being added but none test the case where >1000 spans are inserted to verify the eviction works correctly and retains the newest spans. This is a legitimate missing test coverage concern for newly added functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:68 — No endpoint test exercises optimized pagination for both permitted and unpermitted users

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new pagination logic in organization_auditlogs.py with two code paths: one using OptimizedCursorPaginator when 'optimized_pagination=true' and the user is a superuser or has global access, and another using DateTimePaginator otherwise. This is new nontrivial logic that affects authorization behavior. The finding correctly identifies that there are no tests in the diff for this new endpoint behavior - the test files modified are all for spans/buffer functionality, not for the audit logs endpoint. Testing both permitted and unpermitted user scenarios for this new feature would be important to verify the authorization logic works correctly.
